content: 1. Estrada-Reyes E, Pardo-Castañeda M, Toledo-Bahena M, Lerma-Ortiz M, del Río-Navarro B, and Nava-Ocampo A conducted a case-control study investigating the relationship between food hypersensitivity, the timing of weaning, and family history of allergies in young children diagnosed with atopic dermatitis. This study was published in Allergologia et Immunopathologia in 2007, volume 35, issue 3, pages 101-104. 2. Fall CH, Borja JB, Osmond C, Richter L, Bhargava SK, Martorell R, and colleagues analyzed infant feeding patterns and their association with cardiovascular risk factors in young adulthood. The data was derived from five cohorts in lowand middle-income countries. This research appeared in the International Journal of Epidemiology in 2011, volume 40, issue 1, pages 47-62. 3. Fallani M, Amarri S, Uusijarvi A, Adam R, Khanna S, Aguilera M, and collaborators examined the determinants of the human infant intestinal microbiota following the introduction of the first complementary foods. The study utilized infant samples from five European centers and was published in Microbiology in 2011, volume 157, issue 5, pages 1385-1392. 4. Fawzi WW, Forman MR, Levy A, Graubard BI, Naggan L, and Berendes HW explored the relationship between maternal anthropometry, infant feeding practices, and growth during infancy in Israel. This study was part of the North African Infant Feeding Study and was published in The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition in 1997, volume 65, issue 6, pages 1731-1737. 5. Ferris AG, Beal VA, Laus MJ, and Hosmer DW investigated the effects of feeding practices on fat deposition during early infancy. Their findings were published in Pediatrics in 1979, volume 64, issue 4, pages 397-401. 6. Franks AJ and Jurgensen C studied nutrition and health during the first year of life on a Pacific atoll, specifically Abemama Atoll in the Central Pacific. Their observations were published in Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 1985, volume 79, issue 5, pages 681-684. 7. Okubo H, Miyake Y, Sasaki S, Tanaka K, and Hirota Y examined early-life feeding practices and their influence on later fruit and vegetable intake among Japanese toddlers. This research was part of the Osaka Maternal and Child Health Study and was published in Public Health Nutrition in 2016, volume 19, issue 4, pages 650-657. 8. Hop LT, Gross R, Giay T, Sastroamidjojo S, Schultink W, and Lang NT found that premature complementary feeding was associated with poorer growth outcomes in Vietnamese children. Their study was published in The Journal of Nutrition in 2000, volume 130, issue 11, pages 2683-2690. 9. Imai CM, Gunnarsdottir I, Thorisdottir B, Halldorsson TI, and Thorsdottir I investigated the associations between infant feeding practices before six months of age and body mass index at six years of age. Their findings were published in Nutrients in 2014, volume 6, issue 4, pages 1608-1617. 10. Jimenez-Cruz A, Bacardi-Gascon M, Pichardo-Osuna A, Mandujano-Trujillo Z, and Castillo-Ruiz O studied infant and toddler feeding practices and their association with obesity in low-income families in Mexico. This research was published in the Asia Pacific Journal of Clinical Nutrition in 2010, volume 19, issue 3, pages 316-323. 11. Kanoa BJ, Al-Hindi A, and Lubbad AM examined breastfeeding, complementary feeding, and weaning practices among children up to two years old in the Gaza Strip. This study was conducted in 2021. 12. Mehta UJ, Siega-Riz AM, Herring AH, Adair LS, and Bentley ME found that pregravid body mass index was associated with the early introduction of complementary foods. Their study was published in the Journal of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics in 2012, volume 112, issue 9, pages 1374-1379. 13. Popkin BM, Adair L, Akin JS, Black R, Briscoe J, and Flieger W investigated the relationship between breastfeeding and diarrheal morbidity. Their findings were published in Pediatrics in 1990, volume 86, issue 6, pages 874-882. 14. Rathnayake KM, Satchithananthan A, Mahamithawa S, and Jayawardena R conducted a case-control study in Sri Lanka to identify early-life predictors of preschool overweight and obesity. This study was published in BMC Public Health in 2013, volume 13, issue 1, pages 1-6. 15. Rippey PL, Aravena F, and Nyonator JP explored the health impacts of early complementary food introduction in formula-fed versus breastfed infants. Their findings were published in the Journal of Pediatric Gastroenterology and Nutrition in 2020, volume 70, issue 3, pages 375-380. 16. Robinson S, Marriott L, Crozier S, NC G, CR I, and HM B studied variations in infant feeding practices and their association with body composition in childhood. This research was conducted in 2009. 17. Salahuddin M, Perez A, Ranjit N, Hoelscher D, and Kelder S examined the associations between being large-for-gestational-age, infant feeding practices, and children's body mass index z-score trajectories. Their findings were part of the Early Childhood Longitudinal Study, Birth Cohort, and were published in Clinical Obesity in 2017, volume 7, issue 5, pages 307-315. 18. Škledar MT and Milošević M investigated breastfeeding and the timing of complementary food introduction as predictors of obesity in children. Their study was published in the Central European Journal of Public Health in 2015, volume 23, issue 1, pages 26-31. 19. Thorisdottir B, Gunnarsdottir I, Vidarsdottir AG, Sigurdardottir S, Birgisdottir BE, and Thorsdottir I studied the relationship between infant feeding, vitamin D, and IgE sensitization to food allergens at six years of age in a longitudinal Icelandic cohort. Their findings were published in Nutrients in 2019, volume 11, issue 7, article 1690. 20. Vadiveloo M, Tovar A, Østbye T, and Benjamin-Neelon SE examined the associations between the timing and quality of solid food introduction and infant weight-for-length z-scores at 12 months. This study was part of the Nurture cohort and was published in Appetite in 2019, volume 141, article 104299. 21. Werdani KE, Isnaini N, and Kusumawati Y analyzed the history of children and malnutrition status in Magetan. Their findings were published in Executive Editor in 2019, volume 10, issue 3, page 863. 22. Khatun T, Matabbar MS, Sarker MR, and Hoque A conducted a comparative study on feeding practices and nutrition status among children aged 6-23 months. This research was published in the Journal of Life Sciences in 2014, volume 8, issue 8.
